recipes.name: Beef and Broccoli
recipes.summary: Takeout-style beef and broccoli in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce, on the table in half an hour.
steps: Toss the beef strips with 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 tablespoon soy sauce. Set aside while you make the sauce.
Whisk the sauce ingredients (soy sauce, broth, brown sugar, oyster sauce, cornstarch, sesame oil, garlic and ginger) in a bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the broccoli and water, cover and steam 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Move it to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the hot pan. Sear the beef in a single layer, in two batches if needed, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until browned. Thin strips cook fast and reach 145°F in this time.
Wash your hands and any board that held the raw beef. Return all the beef and the broccoli to the pan, whisk the sauce again and pour it in. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Serve right away over rice.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Slice the beef and mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead; keep them covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked beef and broccoli in sauce for up to 2 months for best quality; the broccoli softens a little. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and spoon over rice or noodles for lunch.

recipes.kids: Slice the beef extra thin and cut the broccoli small. Firm the steak in the freezer for 20 minutes first so it slices easily (a grown-up job).

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce and a gluten-free oyster sauce and broth (check labels).
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces extra-firm tofu, pressed, cubed and browned, in place of the beef.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the steak, cut the broccoli and mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Philly-Style Cheesesteaks
recipes.summary: Thin-sliced steak, soft onions and peppers and melted provolone piled into toasted rolls.
steps: Wrap the steak and freeze it 20 minutes so it firms up. Slice it as thin as you can across the grain, trimming off large pieces of fat.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and lightly browned. Move them to a bowl.

Raise the heat to medium-high and add the rest of the oil. Add the steak in a single layer (in batches if needed) and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Cook 3 to 4 minutes, turning and chopping with the spatula, until browned with no pink left. Thin slices pass 145°F quickly; check a thicker piece with a thermometer.

Wash your hands and the board that held the raw steak. Stir the vegetables back in and divide the filling into 4 piles in the pan. Lay 2 slices of provolone over each pile and let it melt, about 1 minute.
Butter the cut sides of the rolls and toast them in a second pan or under the broiler. Slide a spatula under each pile and turn it into a roll.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Slice the steak and vegetables up to 1 day ahead and keep them in separate covered containers in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze the cooked filling without the rolls for up to 2 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Reheat the filling to 165°F and serve over rice or tucked into a quesadilla.

recipes.kids: Leave the peppers off a kid portion, or serve the meat and cheese on a small slider roll.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve the filling over rice or in gluten-free rolls.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the cheese and butter.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the steak, onion and pepper.

recipes.name: Grilled Steak with Chimichurri
recipes.summary: Sirloin seared hot and topped with a bright Argentine-style parsley, garlic and vinegar sauce.
steps: Stir together the parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar, olive oil, pepper flakes and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Let it stand while you cook so the flavors blend.
Pat the steak dry and season both sides with the kosher salt and pepper. Rub with the oil.
Heat the grill or a heavy skillet over high heat. Cook the steak 4 to 6 minutes per side, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads at least 145°F.
Move the steak to a clean board and let it rest 3 minutes or more before slicing. Slice across the grain.
Spoon the chimichurri over the sliced steak.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Make the chimichurri up to 2 days ahead; keep it covered in the fridge and bring to room temperature before serving.

freezer.text: Freeze raw steaks instead, wrapped well, for 6 to 12 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Slice cold steak over a salad or into wraps with a spoonful of the sauce.

recipes.kids: Slice the steak thin across the grain so it is easy to chew. Offer the sauce on the side.

swaps.meatless: Grill thick slices of portobello mushroom or cauliflower and spoon the chimichurri over them.

prep_day.ahead: Make the chimichurri; season the steak.

recipes.name: Country-Fried Steak with Cream Gravy
recipes.summary: Crisp breaded cube steaks and a peppery milk gravy, a Southern diner classic made at home.
steps: In one shallow dish, mix the flour, salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika. In another, beat the eggs with 1/2 cup milk.
Pat the steaks dry. Dip each in the flour, then the egg, then the flour again, pressing so the coating sticks. Wash your hands.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Fry the steaks 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and an instant-read thermometer reads 145°F. Move them to a rack over a baking sheet and let them rest at least 3 minutes; keep them warm in a 200°F oven if you like.
Pour off all but about 3 tablespoons of the fat, keeping the browned bits. Whisk in 3 tablespoons flour and cook 1 minute over medium heat.
Slowly whisk in 2 cups milk. Simmer 3 to 5 minutes, whisking, until thick. Season with pepper and salt.
Serve the steaks with the gravy spooned over.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Bread the steaks up to 2 hours ahead and keep them on a rack in the fridge.

freezer.text: The crust turns soft after freezing. Freeze raw cube steaks instead for up to 6 months.

leftovers.text: Reheat the steaks on a rack in a 375°F oven to 165°F so the crust crisps again; warm the gravy on the stove.

recipes.kids: Cut each steak into strips for dipping in the gravy.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a 1-to-1 gluten-free flour blend for the coating and the gravy.

prep_day.ahead: Mix the seasoned flour.

recipes.name: Beef Bulgogi Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Korean-style sweet and savory marinated beef, seared fast and served over rice with crunchy vegetables.
steps: Firm the steak in the freezer for 20 minutes, then slice it as thin as you can.
In a bowl, mix the soy sauce, brown sugar, grated pear, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, half the green onions and the pepper. Add the beef, toss and marinate in the fridge 30 minutes or up to 8 hours.
Cook the rice while the beef marinates.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add the beef in a single layer, in batches, letting extra marinade drip off. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until browned and caramelized at the edges. Thin slices pass 145°F quickly; check a thicker piece with a thermometer.
Throw away the leftover marinade. Wash your hands and the board that held the raw beef.
Fill bowls with rice, beef, cucumber and carrot. Top with the rest of the green onions and the sesame seeds.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Marinate the beef up to 8 hours ahead. Cook the rice and cut the vegetables up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze the raw beef in its marinade, flat in a freezer bag, for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight and cook as directed.

leftovers.text: Pack cold rice, beef and vegetables in lunch containers; reheat the beef and rice to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Offer the vegetables on the side. The sweet sauce is often a hit with kids.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.
swaps.meatless: Marinate and sear thin slices of extra-firm tofu or mushrooms instead.

prep_day.ahead: Slice and marinate the beef; cook the rice; slice the cucumber and shred the carrots.

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Beef Barbacoa
recipes.summary: Chuck roast slow-cooked in a tangy chile and spice sauce until it shreds, for tacos, burritos and bowls.
steps: Season the beef chunks with the salt and put them in the slow cooker.
Blend the onion, garlic, green chiles, vinegar, lime juice, chili powder, cumin, oregano, cloves and broth until smooth. Pour over the beef and tuck in the bay leaves.
Cover and cook on low 8 to 9 hours or high 5 to 6 hours. The beef is safe at 145°F, but chuck shreds only after long cooking, when a fork twists through it easily.
Remove the bay leaves. Shred the beef with two forks right in the cooker and stir it into the juices.
Warm the tortillas and serve the beef with cilantro, onion and lime wedges.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Cook up to 3 days ahead; chill it in its juices and reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze shredded beef with some of its juices for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Use leftover barbacoa in burritos, rice bowls or quesadillas; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: The sauce is mild with canned green chiles. Serve plain beef in a tortilla with cheese for picky eaters.

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are naturally free of wheat; check the broth label.

prep_day.ahead: Blend the sauce and cut the beef the night before; start the slow cooker in the morning.

recipes.name: Braised Beef Short Ribs
recipes.summary: Short ribs browned and slow-braised in broth with vegetables until the meat falls off the bone.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Pat the ribs dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the ribs well on all sides in batches, 8 to 10 minutes per batch. Move them to a plate and pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery 5 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 minute.

Stir in the broth, vinegar and Worcestershire, scraping up the browned bits. Return the ribs, bone side up, with any juices. Add the thyme and bay leaves. The liquid should come most of the way up the ribs.
Cover and bake 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender and pulls from the bone. The ribs pass 145°F early; the long cook is for tenderness.
Lift out the ribs. Skim the fat from the sauce and simmer it on the stove 5 to 10 minutes to thicken. Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves and spoon the sauce over the ribs.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Braise a day ahead and chill in the pot. Lift off the hardened fat, then reheat covered in a 325°F oven to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze ribs in their sauce for up to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Shred leftover meat into the sauce and serve over egg noodles or mashed potatoes; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Pull the meat off the bone and shred it for younger children.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free Worcestershire sauce and broth (check labels).

prep_day.ahead: Chop the vegetables; brown the ribs the night before if you like.

recipes.name: Vegetable Beef Soup
recipes.summary: An old-fashioned pot of tender beef, potatoes and garden vegetables in a tomato broth.
equipment: large soup pot or Dutch oven
steps: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in two batches, about 5 minutes per batch. Wash your hands after handling the raw meat.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, broth, water, thyme and bay leaves and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover and simmer 1 hour, until the beef is starting to get tender. It passes 145°F early; the simmer is for tenderness.
Add the potatoes and simmer 20 minutes. Add the green beans, corn and peas and simmer 10 minutes more, until everything is tender.
Remove the bay leaves, taste and add salt if needed.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: The soup tastes even better the next day. Cool it quickly in shallow containers and keep it up to 4 days; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for 2 to 3 months for best quality. The potatoes soften a little. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Pack hot soup in a preheated insulated jar for lunch; reheat it to 165°F first.

recipes.kids: Ladle a kid bowl with extra corn and peas. Serve with crackers or bread for dunking.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label; everything else is naturally free of wheat.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the beef and vegetables.

recipes.name: Bacon-Wrapped Pork Tenderloin
recipes.summary: Two lean tenderloins wrapped in bacon and brushed with a brown sugar and mustard glaze.

ingredients.prep: about 1 1/4 lb each, silver skin trimmed

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a rack on it if you have one.
Pat the tenderloins dry and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Wrap each one in 4 strips of bacon, overlapping slightly, and tuck the ends underneath. Wash your hands.
Stir the brown sugar and mustard together and brush it over the bacon.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the pork reads 145°F. For crisper bacon, broil 2 to 3 minutes at the end, watching closely.
Let the pork rest 5 minutes (at least 3), then slice.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Wrap the tenderloins up to 1 day ahead; brush on the glaze just before roasting.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked sliced pork for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Slice leftovers thin for sandwiches with mustard, or chop them into fried rice; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can help brush on the glaze before it goes in the oven. Wash hands after touching the raw meat.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the mustard and bacon labels.

prep_day.ahead: Trim and wrap the pork.

recipes.name: Smothered Pork Chops
recipes.summary: Bone-in pork chops browned, then simmered in a rich onion and mushroom gravy.
steps: Pat the chops dry. Season with the salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder, then dredge lightly in 1/4 cup flour. Wash your hands.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chops 3 minutes per side. Move them to a plate; they finish cooking later.
Lower the heat to medium and add the butter, onions and mushrooms. Cook 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in 2 tablespoons flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and milk, add the thyme and simmer until it starts to thicken.
Nestle the chops and their juices into the gravy. Cover and simmer gently 12 to 15 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part away from the bone reads 145°F.
Let the chops rest 3 minutes in the pan, then serve with plenty of gravy.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Slice the onions and mushrooms up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze chops in their gravy for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat chops in the gravy to 165°F; slice and serve over rice.

recipes.kids: Cut the meat off the bone and into small pieces. The gravy is great over mashed potatoes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch: skip the dredge, and stir 1 tablespoon cornstarch into the milk to thicken the gravy.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the onions and mushrooms.

recipes.name: Crispy Pork Schnitzel
recipes.summary: Boneless chops pounded thin, breaded and pan-fried golden, served with lemon in the German style.
steps: Lay each chop between sheets of plastic wrap and pound to about 1/4 inch thick. Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Set out three shallow dishes: flour; the eggs beaten with the water; and breadcrumbs. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing lightly. Wash your hands.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until a pinch of crumbs sizzles. Fry 2 cutlets at a time, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and an instant-read thermometer reads 145°F.
Drain on a rack or paper towels and let rest 3 minutes. Repeat with the rest, adding a little oil if the pan looks dry.
Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing and a sprinkle of parsley.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Pound and bread the cutlets up to 4 hours ahead; keep them on a rack in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze breaded, uncooked cutlets on a tray, then bag them, for up to 3 months. Fry from frozen over medium heat, a few minutes longer per side, to 145°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat on a rack in a 375°F oven to 165°F; or slice cold onto a roll with mustard.

recipes.kids: Kids can help with the breading line. Wash hands well afterward.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free flour and crushed gluten-free crackers or crumbs.

prep_day.ahead: Pound and bread the cutlets.

recipes.name: Crispy Pork Carnitas
recipes.summary: Pork shoulder slow-cooked with orange, lime and spices, then shredded and broiled until the edges crisp.
steps: Mix the salt, cumin, oregano and pepper and rub it all over the pork. Put the pork in the slow cooker with the onion, garlic and bay leaves. Wash your hands.

Pour the orange juice, lime juice and broth over the pork and drop in the squeezed orange halves. Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours or high 5 to 6 hours. Pork is safe at 145°F, but shoulder shreds only after long cooking, when a fork twists through it easily.
Lift out the pork and throw away the orange halves and bay leaves. Shred the meat with two forks, discarding large pieces of fat. Skim the fat from the juices.

Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below it. Spread the pork on a rimmed baking sheet and drizzle with 1/2 cup of the juices. Broil 5 to 8 minutes, until the edges are browned and crisp. Stir, add a little more juice and broil a few minutes more if you like.
Serve in warm tortillas with cilantro, onion, lime and salsa.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Cook and shred up to 3 days ahead; keep it in some of the juices. Crisp under the broiler just before serving, heating to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze shredded pork with some juices for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge, then crisp under the broiler.

leftovers.text: Use leftovers in burritos, nachos, rice bowls or scrambled eggs; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Serve plain pork with cheese in a soft tortilla. Let kids squeeze their own lime.

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are naturally free of wheat; check the broth label.

prep_day.ahead: Rub the pork with the spices the night before; start the slow cooker in the morning.

recipes.name: Oven Baby Back Ribs
recipes.summary: Low and slow in the oven with a sweet dry rub, then brushed with barbecue sauce and broiled sticky.
steps: Heat the oven to 275°F. Line two baking sheets with foil.
Pat the ribs dry. On the bone side, slide a butter knife under the thin membrane at one end, grab it with a paper towel and pull it off. This step is optional but makes the ribs more tender.
Mix the rub and pat it all over both racks. Set each rack meaty side up on a baking sheet and cover tightly with foil. Wash your hands.
Bake 2 1/2 hours, until the meat is tender and pulling back from the bone ends. Ribs pass 145°F long before they are tender.
Uncover and carefully pour off the juices. Heat the broiler. Brush the ribs with barbecue sauce and broil 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely, until sticky and browned in spots.
Rest 3 minutes, then cut between the bones and serve with more sauce.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Bake the ribs a day ahead and chill them. To serve, brush with sauce and heat in a 400°F oven to 165°F, about 20 minutes.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked ribs (before saucing) wrapped tightly for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Pull the meat off the bones for barbecue sandwiches; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can mix and pat on the rub. Cut ribs into single bones for small hands.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the barbecue sauce label.

prep_day.ahead: Rub the ribs and wrap them; chill overnight.

recipes.name: Garlic Herb Pork Loin Roast
recipes.summary: A garlic, rosemary and mustard crusted pork loin roasted over potatoes and carrots for an easy Sunday dinner.
equipment: large roasting pan or rimmed baking sheet
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Pat the pork dry.
Mix the garlic, rosemary, thyme, mustard, 2 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper into a paste and rub it over the pork. Wash your hands.
Toss the potatoes, carrots and onion with 1 tablespoon oil and 1/2 teaspoon salt in the roasting pan. Set the pork in the middle, fat side up.
Roast 60 to 75 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the center of the roast reads 145°F. Stir the vegetables halfway through.
Move the roast to a board and let it rest 10 minutes (at least 3). If the vegetables need more color, keep roasting them while the meat rests.
Slice the pork and serve with the vegetables and pan juices.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Rub the roast with the herb paste up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze sliced cooked pork for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Slice leftovers thin for Cuban sandwiches or fried rice; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can toss the vegetables with oil and salt in the pan. Slice the pork thin for younger children.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the mustard label.

prep_day.ahead: Rub the roast; cut the vegetables and keep them in water in the fridge.

recipes.name: Pressed Cuban Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard pressed in a hot skillet until crisp. A great use for leftover pork roast.
equipment: second heavy pan or foil-wrapped brick for pressing

ingredients.prep: or a loaf of Cuban or French bread cut in 4
cooked and thinly sliced (leftover roast works well)

steps: Split the rolls and spread mustard on both cut sides.
Layer each sandwich with a slice of cheese, the pork, the ham, the pickles and another slice of cheese. Close the sandwiches and butter the outsides.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Set the sandwiches in the pan and press them down with a second heavy pan. Cook 4 to 5 minutes per side, pressing firmly, until the bread is crisp, the cheese melts and the center reaches 165°F.
Cut each sandwich in half on the diagonal and serve hot.
recipes.make_ahead: Build the sandwiches up to 4 hours ahead and keep them wrapped in the fridge; press just before serving.

freezer.text: Pressed sandwiches turn soggy when frozen. Freeze sliced leftover pork instead.

leftovers.text: Wrap a pressed half in foil and reheat in a 350°F oven to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Skip the pickles and mustard on a kid sandwich, or serve them on the side.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free rolls and check the ham and mustard labels.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the leftover pork and the pickles.

recipes.name: Pork Meatball Banh Mi
recipes.summary: Vietnamese-style sandwiches: juicy pork meatballs, quick-pickled carrots, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño in a crusty roll.
steps: Stir the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved. Add the carrots and set aside at least 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with foil.
Mix the pork, green onions, garlic, ginger, fish sauce, sugar and panko with your hands just until combined. Roll into 16 balls about 1 1/2 inches across and set them on the sheet. Wash your hands.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center of a meatball reads 160°F.
Toast the bread lightly and spread the insides with mayonnaise. Fill each with 4 meatballs (halve them if you like), drained pickled carrots, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño.
recipes.make_ahead: Pickle the carrots up to 5 days ahead. Shape the meatballs up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze baked meatballs on a tray, then bag them, for 3 to 4 months. Reheat from frozen in a 375°F oven to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Serve leftover meatballs and pickles over rice for lunch; reheat the meatballs to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Leave off the jalapeño. Many kids like the meatballs and carrots in a small roll.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs, fish sauce and bread, or serve the meatballs over rice.

prep_day.ahead: Pickle the carrots; shape the meatballs.

recipes.name: Egg Roll in a Bowl
recipes.summary: All the flavor of an egg roll filling, made in one skillet with ground pork and shredded cabbage.
steps: Cook the pork in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, about 7 minutes. Spoon off extra fat.
Add the sesame oil, onion, garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the coleslaw mix and carrot. Cook 4 to 5 minutes, tossing, until the cabbage wilts but still has some crunch.
Stir in the soy sauce and vinegar. Top with green onions, and hot sauce for anyone who wants it.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge in meal-prep containers.

freezer.text: The cabbage turns watery when frozen. Freeze cooked, seasoned ground pork instead.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and serve over rice, or roll into a tortilla.

recipes.kids: Serve over rice with a few crunchy wonton strips or crackers on top.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces crumbled extra-firm tofu, browned in 1 tablespoon oil.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the whole dish and portion it.

recipes.name: Swedish Meatballs over Egg Noodles
recipes.summary: Tender beef and pork meatballs with a hint of allspice in a creamy gravy, spooned over buttered noodles.
steps: In a large bowl, soak the panko in the milk for 5 minutes. Add the beef, pork, egg, onion, salt, pepper, allspice and nutmeg and mix gently with your hands. Roll into about 30 balls, 1 1/4 inches across. Wash your hands.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the meatballs in batches, turning, about 8 minutes per batch, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F. Move them to a plate.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in salted boiling water by the package directions. Drain and toss with 1 tablespoon butter and the parsley.
Pour off the fat from the skillet. Melt 3 tablespoons butter, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and simmer 3 minutes, until thickened.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the sour cream and Worcestershire. Return the meatballs and warm gently over low heat, without boiling, until hot.
Serve the meatballs and gravy over the noodles.
recipes.make_ahead: Brown the meatballs up to 2 days ahead and keep them in the fridge. Make the gravy and reheat the meatballs in it to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze browned meatballs on a tray, then bag them, for 3 to 4 months. The sour cream gravy can separate when frozen, so make it fresh.

leftovers.text: Reheat meatballs and gravy gently to 165°F, adding a splash of broth.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the meatballs. Wash hands well before and after.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs, flour and Worcestershire, and serve over rice or mashed potatoes.

prep_day.ahead: Roll and brown the meatballs.

recipes.name: Thai-Style Pork Lettuce Wraps
recipes.summary: Inspired by Thai larb: ground pork tossed with lime, fish sauce, shallot and lots of fresh mint and cilantro.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, 6 to 7 minutes.
Add the shallots and garlic and cook 1 minute. Take the pan off the heat.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and pepper flakes together and pour over the pork. Toss in the cilantro, mint and green onions.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and serve with cucumber slices.
recipes.make_ahead: Wash and dry the lettuce and mix the lime dressing up to 1 day ahead.

freezer.text: The fresh herbs do not freeze well. Freeze plain cooked ground pork instead.

leftovers.text: Serve cold or reheated to 165°F over rice; add fresh herbs.

recipes.kids: Go easy on the pepper flakes and offer the filling with rice for kids who prefer it.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the fish sauce label.

prep_day.ahead: Wash the lettuce; juice the limes; pick the herbs.

recipes.name: Loaded Baked Potato Soup
recipes.summary: Creamy potato soup topped like a baked potato with bacon, cheddar, sour cream and green onions.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Lift it out onto paper towels, leaving about 2 tablespoons of fat in the pot.
Add the onion and cook 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then add the potatoes. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes right in the pot for a thick, chunky soup. Stir in the milk, salt and pepper and heat until steaming; do not let it boil hard.
Ladle into bowls and top with bacon, cheddar, sour cream and green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the soup up to 3 days ahead. Keep the toppings separate. Reheat to 165°F over medium-low heat, adding milk to thin.

freezer.text: Potato and milk soups turn grainy when frozen. Make a half batch if you need less.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and pack in a preheated insulated jar with toppings on the side.

recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle on their own toppings.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into the milk in place of the flour; check the broth and bacon labels.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the bacon and chop the onion and potatoes (keep potatoes covered in water in the fridge).

recipes.name: Ham and Cheddar Quiche
recipes.summary: A creamy custard filled with diced ham and sharp cheddar in a flaky crust. Good warm or at room temperature.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Fit the crust into the pie plate and crimp the edge. Set it on a baking sheet.
Whisk the eggs, half-and-half, salt, pepper and nutmeg in a bowl.
Scatter the ham, cheese and green onions in the crust. Pour the egg mixture over.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the center is just set and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F. If the crust edge browns too fast, cover it with strips of foil.
Let the quiche stand 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge. Serve cold, or reheat slices to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the baked, cooled quiche wrapped well for up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat in a 350°F oven to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack a cold wedge for lunch with fruit, or reheat it to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle in the ham and cheese and help whisk.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free crust, or bake it crustless in a greased pie plate for about 35 minutes.

prep_day.ahead: Dice the ham and shred the cheese.

recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes and Ham
recipes.summary: Thin-sliced potatoes and diced ham baked in a creamy cheddar sauce. A smart way to use up holiday ham.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter the baking dish.

Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion 4 minutes. Whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk. Simmer, whisking, until thickened, about 5 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the salt, pepper, mustard and 1 cup of the cheese.
Layer half the potatoes in the dish, scatter the ham over and pour on half the sauce. Repeat with the rest of the potatoes and sauce.
Cover with foil and bake 50 minutes. Uncover, sprinkle with the rest of the cheese and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden. The center should reach 165°F.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead (the sauce keeps the potatoes from browning) and refrigerate. Add 10 to 15 minutes to the covered bake.

freezer.text: Potatoes in cream sauce turn grainy after freezing. This one is best within 4 days.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions to 165°F in the microwave or a covered dish in the oven.

recipes.kids: Kids can layer the potato slices. A grown-up slices the potatoes; a mandoline needs a guard.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3 tablespoons cornstarch in place of the flour, whisked into cold milk; check the ham label.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the casserole and refrigerate it unbaked.

recipes.name: Brown Sugar Glazed Spiral Ham
recipes.summary: A fully cooked spiral ham warmed slowly and finished with a brown sugar, mustard and orange glaze. Plenty for a crowd and for leftovers.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Set the ham cut side down in the pan and add the water. Cover tightly with foil so it does not dry out.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes per pound, about 1 1/2 hours for a 7-pound ham, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part, not touching bone, reads 120°F.
Meanwhile, simmer the glaze ingredients in a small saucepan 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until slightly thick.

Raise the oven to 400°F. Uncover the ham, brush it all over with half the glaze, letting some run between the slices, and bake 10 minutes. Brush with the rest and bake 5 to 10 minutes more, until glossy and the ham reaches 140°F.
Let it rest 10 minutes, then cut along the bone to release the slices. Spoon the pan juices over.
recipes.make_ahead: Mix the glaze up to 1 week ahead and keep it in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze sliced leftover ham for 1 to 2 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Use leftover ham in Ham and Cheddar Quiche, Scalloped Potatoes and Ham, sandwiches or split pea soup. Save the bone for soup. Reheat leftovers to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can brush on the glaze with a grown-up close by; the pan and oven are hot.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the ham and mustard labels.

prep_day.ahead: Mix the glaze.

recipes.name: Herb-Roasted Turkey Breast
recipes.summary: A bone-in turkey breast with garlic herb butter under the skin. Thanksgiving flavor without the whole bird, and plenty of leftovers.
equipment: roasting pan with rack, or a 9-by-13-inch pan
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. If the turkey was frozen, thaw it in the fridge, allowing about 1 day per 4 to 5 pounds.
Mash the butter with the garlic, rosemary, thyme, sage, salt and pepper.
Pat the turkey dry. Gently loosen the skin with your fingers and spread half the butter under it, right on the meat. Rub the rest over the skin. Wash your hands.
Scatter the onion in the pan, set the turkey on top (on a rack if you have one) and pour in the broth.
Roast 1 3/4 to 2 1/4 hours, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part, not touching bone, reads 165°F. If the skin browns too fast, tent it loosely with foil.
Let the turkey rest 15 minutes before carving so the juices settle. Slice the meat off the bone, then across the grain.
recipes.make_ahead: Roast a day ahead, chill the meat within 2 hours, and slice it cold; reheat covered with a splash of broth to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze sliced turkey with a little broth for 2 to 6 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Use leftovers in Turkey Wild Rice Soup, Turkey Tetrazzini or club sandwiches within 3 to 4 days.

recipes.kids: Kids can help mash the herb butter. Wash hands after touching the raw turkey.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil in place of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Thaw the turkey; mix the herb butter.

recipes.name: Creamy Turkey Wild Rice Soup
recipes.summary: A Minnesota-style creamy soup with nutty wild rice, vegetables and leftover roast turkey.

ingredients.prep: cooked, skin and bone removed, diced (about 3 cups; leftover roast turkey works)

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots, celery and mushrooms 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth, then add the wild rice, thyme and pepper.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, cover and simmer 45 to 55 minutes, until the rice is tender and some grains have split open.
Stir in the turkey and half-and-half and heat until the soup is steaming and reaches 165°F. Do not let it boil hard after the cream goes in. Taste and add salt if needed.
recipes.make_ahead: Make up to 3 days ahead. The rice soaks up broth, so thin with more broth when reheating to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality; the cream may separate a little, so stir well when reheating to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and pack in a preheated insulated jar.

recipes.kids: Serve with crackers or a dinner roll. Dice the vegetables small for younger kids.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the half-and-half in place of the flour; check the broth label.

prep_day.ahead: Dice the vegetables and the cooked turkey.

recipes.name: Turkey Tetrazzini
recipes.summary: A creamy, cheesy baked spaghetti with turkey, mushrooms and peas, the classic answer to holiday leftovers.

ingredients.prep: cooked, skin and bone removed, diced (about 3 cups; leftover roast turkey works)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter the baking dish. Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water 2 minutes less than the package says; drain.
Melt 4 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion 8 minutes, until browned and soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and milk and simmer, whisking, until thick, about 5 minutes. Season with salt, pepper and thyme.
Off the heat, stir in the turkey, peas, 1/2 cup Parmesan and the spaghetti. Spread in the dish.
Mix the panko, melted butter and the rest of the Parmesan and sprinkle over. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until bubbling, golden on top and 165°F in the center.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead without the topping and refrigerate. Add the topping and bake 35 to 40 minutes, to 165°F in the center.

freezer.text: Freeze the unbaked casserole, without the topping, wrapped well for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, add the topping and bake to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions to 165°F with a splash of milk.

recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle on the crumb topping. Chicken works the same way.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free spaghetti, flour and crumbs, and check the broth.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the casserole and refrigerate it unbaked.

recipes.name: Turkey Club Sandwiches
recipes.summary: Triple-decker toast stacked with roast turkey, ham, crisp bacon, lettuce and tomato.

ingredients.prep: cooked and thinly sliced (leftover roast turkey works well)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the bacon on a foil-lined baking sheet and bake 15 to 18 minutes, until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread and spread one side of each slice with mayonnaise.
For each sandwich: top a slice of toast with turkey and ham, then a second slice, mayo side up. Add 2 strips of bacon, lettuce and tomato, and finish with a third slice, mayo side down.
Push 4 toothpicks into each sandwich and cut it into 4 triangles with a serrated knife. Remove the toothpicks before giving it to young children.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake the bacon up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge; warm it briefly or use it cold.

freezer.text: The lettuce and tomato do not freeze. Freeze sliced turkey on its own instead.

recipes.kids: Make a simpler double-decker for small hands, and leave off whatever they do not like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread and check the bacon and ham labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Mayonnaise has no milk; check the bread label.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the bacon and slice the turkey and tomato.

recipes.name: Turkey Cobb Salad
recipes.summary: Rows of turkey, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese over crisp romaine with a mustard vinaigrette.

ingredients.prep: cooked, skin and bone removed, diced (leftover roast turkey works well)

steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 12 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Cool in ice water, then peel and chop.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and crumble.
Shake the vinegar, mustard, salt, pepper and oil in a jar.
Spread the romaine on a platter. Arrange the turkey, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomato and blue cheese in rows on top. Sprinkle with chives.
Drizzle with some of the dressing and pass the rest.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the eggs and bacon and mix the dressing up to 3 days ahead. Dice the avocado just before serving.

freezer.text: Salads do not freeze.

leftovers.text: Keep leftover toppings separate from the lettuce and dressing; pack them for lunch the next day.

recipes.kids: Serve the toppings in little piles and let kids pick. Swap the blue cheese for cheddar.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the bacon and mustard labels.

prep_day.ahead: Hard-cook the eggs, cook the bacon, wash the lettuce and mix the dressing.

recipes.name: Lamb Kofta Pitas with Yogurt Sauce
recipes.summary: Middle Eastern-style spiced lamb skewers or patties with fresh herbs, tucked into warm pita with cucumber yogurt sauce.
steps: Stir the yogurt, cucumber, garlic, lemon juice and salt together and chill.

Mix the lamb, onion, garlic, parsley, mint, spices, salt and pepper with your hands until well combined. Shape into 8 long ovals about 4 inches long (around skewers if you have them). Wash your hands.
Heat the grill or broiler to medium-high. Cook the kofta 10 to 12 minutes, turning a few times, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Tuck 2 kofta into each warm pita with tomato, onion and a big spoonful of yogurt sauce.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape the kofta and make the sauce up to 1 day ahead; keep them covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze shaped raw kofta on a tray, then bag them, for 3 to 4 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking.

leftovers.text: Slice leftover kofta over rice or a salad with the sauce; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Make small round patties instead of long kofta and serve with pita triangles for dipping in the sauce.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve over rice or salad instead of pita.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt, or hummus, for the sauce.
swaps.meatless: Use falafel or grilled vegetables in the pitas.

prep_day.ahead: Shape the kofta; make the yogurt sauce.

recipes.name: Greek Lamb Burgers with Feta
recipes.summary: Juicy lamb patties seasoned with oregano and garlic, topped with feta, cucumber and a lemony yogurt spread.
steps: Stir the yogurt, lemon juice and dill together.
Mix the lamb, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper gently with your hands. Shape into 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick with a dimple in the center. Wash your hands.
Heat the grill or skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Toast the buns. Spread with the yogurt sauce and build the burgers with lettuce, a patty, feta, cucumber and onion.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge with wax paper between.

freezer.text: Freeze raw patties with wax paper between for 3 to 4 months. Thaw in the fridge or cook from frozen, adding a few minutes per side.

leftovers.text: Crumble a leftover patty into a pita with salad; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Make slider-size patties, still cooked to 160°F. Feta is salty and tangy; offer it on the side.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns or wrap in lettuce.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta and use mayonnaise with lemon and dill for the spread.

prep_day.ahead: Shape the patties; mix the spread; slice the cucumber and onion.

recipes.name: Moussaka
recipes.summary: The Greek layered bake: roasted eggplant, a cinnamon-scented lamb and tomato sauce, and a thick golden white sauce on top.

ingredients.prep: about 1 pound each, sliced 1/3 inch thick

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Brush the eggplant slices with the oil, lay them on two baking sheets and sprinkle with salt. Roast 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and browned. Lower the oven to 350°F.

Meanwhile, cook the lamb and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off the fat. Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, salt and pepper and simmer 15 minutes, until thick.

For the white sauce, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer, whisking, until thick, about 5 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in the nutmeg and salt, then the egg, quickly so it does not scramble, and half the Parmesan.
Layer half the eggplant in the baking dish, then all the meat sauce, then the rest of the eggplant. Spread the white sauce over the top and sprinkle with the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until golden on top and 165°F in the center. Let it rest 20 minutes before cutting so the layers set.
recipes.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate. Bake about 60 minutes from cold, to 165°F in the center.

freezer.text: Freeze baked, cooled squares wrapped well for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Moussaka is even better the next day. Reheat squares to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Many kids like it as "Greek lasagna." Serve a smaller square with bread.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the cold milk in place of the flour.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans of drained lentils in place of the lamb.

prep_day.ahead: Roast the eggplant and make the meat sauce.

recipes.name: Lamb Keema with Peas
recipes.summary: A homey South Asian-style dish of spiced ground lamb, tomato and green peas, ready for rice or warm naan.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 6 to 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the lamb and raise the heat to medium-high. Cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, about 7 minutes. Spoon off extra fat.
Stir in the curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne and salt and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and water. Cover and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in the peas and simmer 3 minutes more.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the yogurt. Top with cilantro and serve with rice or naan.
recipes.make_ahead: Keema keeps 3 days in the fridge and tastes even better the next day. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze in portions for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and stuff into a pita or serve over rice.

recipes.kids: Leave out the cayenne. Serve with plain yogurt on the side to cool each bite.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with rice.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the yogurt or use a dairy-free one.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans of drained lentils or chickpeas in place of the lamb.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the whole dish and portion it.

recipes.name: Rosemary Garlic Lamb Chops
recipes.summary: Loin chops marinated in rosemary, garlic and lemon, then seared hot for a special but easy dinner.
steps: Mix the oil, garlic, rosemary, lemon juice and mustard in a shallow dish. Add the chops and turn to coat. Let stand 30 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate up to 8 hours.
Season the chops with the salt and pepper.
Heat a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chops 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 145°F.
Move them to a clean plate and let rest 3 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: Marinate the chops in the fridge up to 8 hours ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze raw chops instead, wrapped well, for 6 to 9 months. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Slice leftover meat off the bone into a pita or over a salad; reheat to 165°F if serving warm.

recipes.kids: Cut the meat off the bone into bite-size pieces. Some kids like to hold the chop by the bone.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the mustard label.

prep_day.ahead: Marinate the chops.

recipes.name: Baked Turkey Meatballs
recipes.summary: Tender, Parmesan-flecked turkey meatballs baked on a sheet pan. Serve with marinara over pasta or in subs.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with foil and oil it lightly.
In a large bowl, soak the panko in the milk 5 minutes. Add the turkey, egg, Parmesan, garlic, parsley, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper and mix gently with your hands.
Roll into about 30 balls, 1 1/2 inches across (wet hands help), and set them on the sheet. Wash your hands.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center of a meatball reads 165°F.
Warm the marinara in a large pot, add the meatballs and simmer a few minutes. Serve over pasta or in rolls.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake up to 3 days ahead and keep in the fridge. Reheat in the sauce to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze baked meatballs on a tray, then bag them, for 3 to 4 months. Reheat from frozen in simmering sauce to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Make meatball subs with leftovers and a little cheese; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the meatballs. Wash hands well before and after.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs and check the marinara label.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the Parmesan and use unsweetened plant milk.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the meatballs.

recipes.name: Turkey White Bean Chili
recipes.summary: A mild green chili with ground turkey, white beans, corn and cumin, topped with cheese and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and jalapeño and cook 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, chili powder and salt and stir 1 minute.
Add the green chiles, beans and broth. Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the chili. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the corn and simmer 5 minutes more. Stir in the lime juice.
Top bowls with cheese and cilantro.
recipes.make_ahead: Make up to 4 days ahead. Reheat to 165°F, adding a splash of broth.

freezer.text: Freeze without toppings for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and pack in a preheated insulated jar, or spoon over a baked potato.

recipes.kids: Seed the jalapeño well, or leave it out. Serve with tortilla chips for scooping.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese; top with avocado.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the chili and portion it.

recipes.name: Juicy Turkey Burgers
recipes.summary: Lean ground turkey kept moist with grated onion and Worcestershire, grilled or pan-cooked.
steps: Mix the turkey, grated onion, Worcestershire, panko, garlic powder, salt and pepper gently with your hands. The mixture will be soft.
Shape into 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick with a dimple in the center. Wash your hands.

Brush the grill grate or skillet with the oil and heat over medium. Cook the patties 6 to 7 minutes per side, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 165°F. Turkey needs a little more cooking than beef, so go by the thermometer.
Add the cheese for the last minute and cover to melt. Toast the buns and build the burgers.
recipes.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge with wax paper between.

freezer.text: Freeze raw patties with wax paper between for 3 to 4 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking.

leftovers.text: Crumble a leftover patty over a salad or into a wrap; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Make sliders; they cook in about 4 minutes per side, still to 165°F.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs, Worcestershire and buns.

prep_day.ahead: Shape the patties; slice the tomato.
